subject.title: Codex-OAuth models fail over incorrectly — sibling model with healthy per-model quota still drops to non-codex fallback

question: Should OpenClaw make the direct `openclaw` Codex responses runtime a supported fallback for Codex-OAuth models by adding `functions.*` Harmony tool-call parsing, or should maintainers keep the app-server path canonical and fix the false 429 upstream first?
rationale: Both paths touch provider routing and fallback semantics that AGENTS.md treats as compatibility-sensitive, and the issue includes live user evidence but not a maintainer-approved default-route decision or a proven upstream Codex root cause.

options.title: Add the direct-runtime adapter first
options.body: Extend the existing Harmony repair seam for `functions.<tool>` targets, keep app-server default for now, and use live OAuth proof before considering default route changes.

options.title: Fix app-server behavior upstream first
options.body: Keep Codex app-server as the only supported default and investigate the WebSocket/session reuse or server-side 429 behavior in the upstream Codex runtime before changing OpenClaw direct routing.

options.title: Land only quota bookkeeping for now
options.body: Treat the linked quota PR as a partial mitigation and defer direct-runtime tool support, leaving this issue open for the remaining app-server fallback case.

recommendation.title: Add the direct-runtime adapter first
recommendation.body: Extend the existing Harmony repair seam for `functions.<tool>` targets, keep app-server default for now, and use live OAuth proof before considering default route changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans OpenAI/Codex provider auth, quota bookkeeping, and current release/provider behavior where this owner history is strongest.
